name: subdivide_hidden_face
description: Frozen reference behaviour: subdividing a cage that contains a hidden face never drops the hiding and never splits it across children — the hidden face comes through as exactly ONE hidden face, because it is EXCLUDED FROM THE OPERATION rather than merely 'preserved'. The polygon counts say so: 21, not 24 (five faces got four children each, the sixth was carried through untouched). Undo restores the geometry and the mark together as a single entry.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted): one process per branch. Four selection branches plus a control that the mark is there at all, plus an undo leg driven at the top level.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (case script + per-case result JSON live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: Four subdivision types were tried on a clean cage first; all four take 6 quads to 24, so the 21 below is not a type artefact. The undo leg had to be driven at the TOP level rather than from inside the case script, because an undo issued inside a script consumes the whole script — so it is the one row here with no per-case result JSON, only a transcript. Recorded as such.

rig.comment: A one-segment cube: six quads, eight vertices. Every face is a quad, so a subdivision gives each face exactly four children and the branch counts separate cleanly.

counts_that_separate_the_readings.note: A test that only asserts 'hiding did not get lost' passes under two of these three. Count.

rows.role: baseline — the mark is there before anything is baked

rows.select_all_note: Selecting everything yields FIVE, not six — the hidden face cannot be selected at all. That is itself part of the mechanism.

rows.role: no-op — the only face named is the one the operation skips, so nothing happens

undo.law: one entry; geometry and mark are restored together, not as two separate steps
undo.evidence_note: No per-case result JSON for this leg — see the provenance note on why it had to be driven at the top level.

conclusion.law: Hidden faces are EXCLUDED FROM THE OPERATION, per component type. Never 0 hidden (dropped), never 4 (children of a subdivided hidden face) — always exactly 1.
conclusion.arithmetic: 21 = 5 faces x 4 children + 1 untouched hidden face.
conclusion.the_task_premise_this_kills: The plan behind 0632 turned on a distinction between a WHOLE-mesh bake (which might rebuild the mesh wholesale and lose the mark) and a SELECTION-restricted bake (which might carry unmarked cage faces through intact). The reference does not distinguish them: both simply skip the hidden face, and both give 21.

not_covered.why: That command aborts on a non-subpatch cage, so this capture never exercised it. Absent, not negative.

classification.detail: Task 0632 landed on 2026-08-09 and the operand divergence is CLOSED: vibe3d now excludes hidden faces from the subdivision operand, so all four engine branches answer 21 / exactly 1 hidden, matching the reference down to the surviving face's index (20). What remains is one output-ORDERING difference on the one-visible-face row (surviving index 4 here, 5 there) and one row that cannot be expressed here at all — both recorded below with their reasons rather than folded into the parity claim.

vibe3d_measured.comment: Re-measured 2026-08-09 against the landed 0632. Every number here is what a live vibe3d answers today; the rows that changed when 0632 landed are marked `closed_by`.

classification.why_all_selected_matches: It matched even BEFORE 0632, and not for the reference's reason: hiding a face clears its selected bit, so selecting everything yields five here too, and the five-face selection then drove the selective branch to 21 / 1. That agreement was reached by the SELECTION MASK, and it disappeared the moment nothing was selected. Since 0632 the row is over-determined — mask and exclusion rule now agree — which is why the nothing-selected row, where only the exclusion rule can produce 21, is the one that actually tests the law.
classification.why_one_visible_face_index_is_pinned_to_: Both engines end with 9 polygons and exactly 1 hidden; only the surviving face's INDEX differs (4 here, 5 there). That is output ordering, not semantics, so the REFERENCE's index is not a parity requirement — but OURS is still pinned, at 4, as an ordering-regression guard. Two different claims that an earlier wording ran together by saying the index was 'not asserted': the row's `hidden_index_after` (5) is not asserted, `vibe3d_measured.one_visible_face_selected.hidden_index_after` (4) is. Re-measured after 0632: still 4 here and 5 there, so this difference is untouched by the operand fix and stays a stated difference rather than a silently updated number.
classification.unrepresentable_here: 'Only the hidden face selected' cannot be expressed: a hidden face cannot be selected, so the attempt yields an empty selection and degenerates into the nothing-selected branch. Re-measured after 0632, that degenerate branch reads 21 / 1 where the reference's own row is a 6 / 1 no-op — so this row still differs, and it differs because the SELECTION is inexpressible, not because the operand law does.
classification.retire_when: RETIRED. 0632 landed (`subdivide: hidden faces leave the operand, and the mark survives the rebuild`) and excluded hidden faces from the subdivision operand; the nothing-selected branch went to 21 / 1 hidden at index 20 and the marker assertion fired exactly as designed, reading `DIVERGENCE CLOSED`. `expected_divergence` is now false and the row is a live parity assertion. Flipping this back to true is NOT a way to silence a regression: the marker branch then demands a disagreement we no longer have and fails just as loudly.
